title: 40-gallon planted community tank

photo.caption: Full tank, day 11 of the cycle (10/13). Still a light haze from the bacterial bloom.

setup: Oase canister filter with built-in heater
Nutrient plant soil capped with sand
Chlorinated city tap water (tap: pH 7.8, KH 180, GH 125)
Continuum Aquatics Fraction, 4 ml per water change
Microbe-Lift Nite-Out II, 20 ml daily during the cycle
Zeolite root tabs at each plant base (added 10/07)
8-in-1 test strips plus a separate ammonia test. Strip readings are color estimates; the strip's nitrite scale steps 0, 1, 5, 10 ppm.

fish.name: Platy
fish.note: 3 added 10/04; more added 10/10. Colors seen: yellow, red, black with yellow fins.

fish_total_note: Up to about 19 fish in total. Exact count by species still being confirmed. One fish is white with black spots (dalmatian platy or molly?).

plants.count: About 11 to 15 plants of varying sizes

species.name: Java fern
species.note: several, including the narrow wavy-leaf type

species.name: Cryptocoryne (likely wendtii)
species.note: green and brown-red; some leaves melting since replanting

species.name: Anubias
species.note: broad dark leaves by the driftwood

species.name: Fine-leaved stem plant
species.note: front right; type to be confirmed

species.name: Floating plants
species.note: from 10/14 close-ups: Amazon frogbit (round shiny leaves, long roots), dwarf water lettuce (velvety blue-green rosettes), red root floaters (small leaves turning red, red roots), and possibly salvinia; growing fast with long roots

plants.species_note: Names are from the photo and not yet confirmed. Corrections welcome!

hardscape.note: reddish-brown wood; type unknown. White fuzz on parts of it (see close-ups).
large grey holey rock, back right; type unknown (Seiryu-style?).
a few smooth stones on the sand
glass octopus figure; ship ornament at the back

timeline: Cycle started. First Nite-Out II dose; no fish.
First fish: 4 zebra danios and 3 platys (switched to a fish-in cycle).
KH dropped 80 to 40 and pH 6.8 to 6.2 overnight.
First ammonia and nitrite readings (0.5 ppm each).
50% water change. Plants re-anchored, root tabs added. Nitrite back to 0; KH back to 80.
KH and pH dropped again overnight (80 to 40, 7.2 to 6.2).
Milky water (bacterial bloom). KH 80 and pH 6.8 held for two days.
About 12 more fish added mid-cycle, not quarantined. KH and pH dropped again that evening.
Ammonia and nitrite still 0 the morning after. KH 40, pH 6.2.
KH down to 20 by morning. 50% water change that evening took KH back to 80 and pH to 6.8.
KH 80 and pH 6.8 held overnight. Ammonia and nitrite 0 for the 6th morning in a row (3rd with all the fish).
questions: KH and pH keep dropping overnight (KH 80 to 40, pH 6.8 to 6.2) even though the tap water is KH 180, pH 7.8. We think the plant soil and driftwood are pulling them down. Crushed coral is on order. What else has worked for you?
Stocking: zebra danios, platys, angelfish, and two dwarf gouramis in a 40-gallon, added while the tank is still cycling. Any compatibility or overstocking concerns?
Nitrate has read 0 for about a week in a heavily planted tank. Normal with this many plants, or a strip problem?
White cottony fuzz is growing on parts of the driftwood (see the close-ups). We're treating it as the usual new-wood biofilm and leaving it. Agree? Anything that would eat it in this stocking?
GH swings between 50 and 125 on the strips. Has anyone seen strips this jumpy?
Can anyone identify the plants and the grey holey rock? If the rock is a Seiryu-type stone it should push KH up, not down, which makes the KH drops more puzzling.
